newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

NO MAGIC WAND WARNS BLAIR The Labour leader Tony Blair, launching his manifesto today, warned the electorate not to expect any miracles to be performed by a Labour government, but the implementation of a realistic programme. With Labour's lead in the polls increased, Blair said that if his government failed to keep its pledges it would pay the price.
HERMES CAUSES STIR WITH CHAIRMEN RULE

A code drawn up by Hermes chief Alistair Ross Goobey, and sent to the chairmen of Britain's top 1000 public companies, has caused controversy with its proposal that retiring chief executives should not step straight into the role of chairman. The Hermes code, most of which has received widespread support, lays down how the fund management giant will vote the 16 billion stg of British shares which it manages for the Post Office and BT schemes.
FOOTSIE SET TO STAND FIRM AGAINST US SLIDE

The FT-SE 100 Index looks set to continue its resilience at around the 4200 level, despite the General Election campaign. The Footsie has reacted much better than continental European markets in the face of the 8 percent fall on Wall Street.
SUMMER COMES EARLY FOR TOUR OPERATORS

Summer holiday bookings are up 18 percent on last year to February, while the number of holidays has increased by five percent. Airtours chief executive Harry Coe has said consumers would be well advised to buy from the brochure.
